# What a hand-built hook set does, and where ws does it

People who've wired their own hooks into Claude Code or OpenCode usually end up with the same kinds of hook: a shell
guard, a secrets guard, a protected-files guard, a staging guard, a claims check, an alert. This page maps each kind to
the ws rule or guard that does the same job, and says what happens when that check crashes. It's for anyone moving a
hand-built set to ws, and for anyone who wants to know what ws covers without reading the code.

Each row is one class of hook (a user-level hook that ...). The status says where its job lives now:

- **covered**: a ws rule or guard does it. The last column names the test that sends the same sample call to the ws
  side and checks the decision.
- **planned**: ws will do it; the row names the wave. No row may stay planned at release.
- **estate**: the job belongs to one person's own setup (their dashboards, their folder layout, their queue), so it
  lives in that person's private config and not in ws. ws gives the place to hang it (a `deny_commands` pattern, a
  guard, a hook of your own), and the reason is in the row.
- **dropped**: ws has no counterpart, and the reason says why.

The *If it crashes* column is the fail mode: **blocks** means a crash or a doubt denies the call (the gate fails
closed); **never-blocks** means the hook only advises or records, so a crash is one stderr line.

All of ws's hooks reach the runner through one command, the [resident gate](gate.md#the-resident-gate), so each
covered row runs in the same fixed order: the policy's rules first, then the guards that are on, lowest priority first
(see [guards](guards.md#the-order-guards-run-in)).

| # | Class | What the hook does | In ws | Status | If it crashes | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `irreversible-shell` | Blocks irreversible shell commands: recursive deletes of system folders, forced pushes, disk formatting | `[gate] deny_commands` (the default list covers these; add your own patterns) | covered | blocks | `test_parity_irreversible_shell_commands` |
| 2 | `credential-reads` | Blocks reads of credential files and key stores, by a shell command or by a file tool | `[gate] deny_read`, applied to shell words, Read, Grep and Glob alike | covered | blocks | `test_parity_credential_reads` |
| 3 | `terminal-session-keys` | Stops one session sending keystrokes to, or killing, another terminal-multiplexer session | A `deny_commands` pattern you add (such as `tmux kill-*`); which sessions to protect depends on how you work | estate | blocks | none |
| 4 | `sealed-folders` | Keeps a session out of folders sealed off for a class of repository (reads and writes) | `[gate] deny_read` and `allow_write`, and the sandbox's `denyRead`; the list of sealed folders is yours | covered | blocks | `test_parity_sealed_folders` |
| 5 | `guardrail-files` | Lets the files that hold the guardrails be edited only by the session that owns them | ws protects its own policy, settings, hooks and folders from the edit tools and from shell redirects; the `config-guard` guard does the same for files and folders you name, edited only from the owner folders you list | covered | blocks | `test_parity_guardrail_files`, `test_parity_config_guard` |
| 6 | `bulk-staging` | Blocks staging the whole tree (`git add -A`, `git add .`, `git commit -a`) | the `bulk-staging` guard | covered | blocks | `test_parity_bulk_staging` |
| 7 | `claims` | Checks a claim that a commit is merged or pushed before the message goes | the `claims` guard | covered | blocks | `test_parity_claims` |
| 8 | `session-context` | Tells a new session which state and hand-off files exist | the `session-context` guard | covered | never-blocks | `test_parity_session_context` |
| 9 | `skill-gate` | Makes a session load a skill before it writes certain files | the `skill-gate` guard | covered | blocks | `test_parity_skill_gate` |
| 10 | `spawn-cap` | Caps how many subagents run at once | the `spawn-cap` guard | covered | blocks | `test_parity_spawn_cap` |
| 11 | `resume-cap` | Stops a conductor resuming a subagent that has grown past a token limit or been resumed twice | none (dropped, reason: no replay row or incident asked for it) | dropped | never-blocks | none |
| 12 | `test-weakening` | Stops a session making tests pass by skipping or weakening them | the `test-weakening` guard | covered | blocks | `test_parity_test_weakening` |
| 13 | `launch-from-main` | Refuses to launch isolated agents or workflows from anywhere but a repository's main checkout | the `guard-launch` guard: a workflow, or an agent that asks for a worktree, starts only from a repository's main checkout | covered | blocks | `test_parity_launch_from_main` |
| 14 | `workflow-fresh` | Checks that a workflow definition is current before it runs | none; it belongs to one workflow tool | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 15 | `phone-alert` | Pushes a phone notification when a session needs input or finishes | `ws notify alert`, written into the Notification and Stop hooks by `ws install` | covered | never-blocks | `test_parity_phone_alert` |
| 16 | `permission-queue` | Puts a permission prompt in a personal queue and closes it when answered | none; the queue is one person's tool (the alert in row 15 still fires) | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 17 | `event-feed` | Sends session events to a personal dashboard | none; the dashboard is one person's | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 18 | `corrections` | Captures corrections the person makes, for later review | none; the review process is one person's | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 19 | `trigger-phrases` | Detects trigger phrases in a prompt and routes them | none; the phrases and routes are one person's | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 20 | `incident-nudge` | Nudges after an incident | none; it names one person's incident process | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 21 | `usage-log` | Logs token usage for a personal dashboard | none; `ws run` writes a [run record](stores.md) for each headless job, and interactive usage stays in the runner's own transcript | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 22 | `status-line` | Draws a custom status line | none; the status line is the runner's own setting | estate | never-blocks | none |
| 23 | `syntax-check` | Checks that a file parses right after a session writes it | the `syntax-check` guard (a finding is a message to the model, never a block) | planned (wave 2b) | never-blocks | none |
| 24 | `force-push-main` | Blocks a force-push to, or deletion of, the main branch on a remote | a `deny_commands` rule or a guard, decided in wave 2b | planned (wave 2b) | blocks | none |
| 25 | `env-file-write` | Blocks a shell command that writes a secret `.env` file | a `deny_commands` rule or a guard, decided in wave 2b | planned (wave 2b) | blocks | none |
| 26 | `scheduled-branch-move` | Blocks a headless job moving the branch of a main checkout | a guard that reads the job marker, decided in wave 2b | planned (wave 2b) | blocks | none |
| 27 | `commit-wall` | Scans the staged diff and the commit message for patterns the person supplies | a commit hook installed by `core.hooksPath` (wave 3) | planned (wave 3) | blocks | none |
| 28 | `test-run-discipline` | Requires test commands to run in the foreground through a wrapper that serialises and bounds them | none; the wrapper is one person's tool (a `deny_commands` pattern can ask for yours) | estate | blocks | none |
| 29 | `duplicate-session` | Warns when two live sessions share a session id or a folder | none; it reads one person's session files | estate | never-blocks | none |

The ws guards with no row above are ones nobody asked for in a hand-built set: `dev-server` (stops a second dev server
starting), `checkout-pin` (keeps work in worktrees) and `record-calls` (records calls for [replay](gate.md)). They're
off or on in `[guards] on`, like the rest.

## Swapping the hook layer for another runner's

The table doesn't change when the runner does. One adapter module owns the translation: `src/ws/adapters/claude_code.py`
or `src/ws/adapters/opencode.py` turns the policy into that runner's own config and parses that runner's hook payload
into a neutral call, and `ws gate` judges the call. To move to a third runner, add a module to `src/ws/adapters/` (the
contract is in that folder's docstring) and list in its `CANNOT_CHECK` every check it can't enforce; `ws run` then
refuses a job whose policy needs one, so a gap is a refusal and never a silent allow.

## How the rows are kept true

`tests/test_hook_parity.py` reads `docs/reference/hook-parity.toml`. A `covered` row must name a test in that file, and
each test sends one sample call that a hand-built hook would stop (and one it would let through) to the ws side. The
tests fail if a row has no test or a bad status or fail mode, if a test has no row, or if this page isn't what the
script writes from the table. Checking a real hook inventory is up to whoever keeps one: `missing(names)` returns the
names that no row has, so a private check can call it with its own list.

A row can move from `estate` or `dropped` to `covered` when ws grows the rule. Moving the other way needs a reason in
the row.
